title: Notification center
desc: Push events such as DDNS changes, certificate expiry, WAF blocks and process failures to channels like Telegram, email and WeCom
noChannels: No channels yet. Add one to receive notifications
confirmDeleteChannel: Delete this channel? Rules referencing it will no longer push to it
noRules: No rules yet. Add a rule to choose which events are pushed to which channels
headersPlaceholder: One per line, in the format Key: Value
fromPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the username
signHelp: Fill in when the bot has "signing" enabled; otherwise leave empty
eventsPlaceholder: Select events; wildcards such as ddns.* are also accepted
silenceHelp: Events of the same type from the same source are pushed only once within this period; 0 disables deduplication
secretSet: Already set; leave empty to keep it

critical.name: Critical failures
critical.desc: DDNS, certificate renewal, upstream, process, backup and container failures

cert.name: Certificate expiry
cert.desc: Certificate nearing expiry or failing to renew

address.name: Address changes
address.desc: Public IP or STUN mapped address changes

health.name: Service health
health.desc: Upstream up/down, container exits and process exits

security.name: Security & sign-ins
security.desc: Failed and successful sign-ins, sign-ins from new addresses, bans and access to sensitive content

changes.name: Configuration changes
changes.desc: Every configuration change made in the admin console

updates.name: Updates
updates.desc: Gately security updates and new versions, plus new versions of managed programs and container images

serverNameHelp: Shown in the title and body of every notification so you can tell which server sent it; leave empty to use the hostname (this machine: {host}). Webhook templates can use the {'{'}server{'}'} variable.
proxyGlobalHelp: Default proxy for all channels; each channel can set its own or connect directly. Supports http://, https:// and socks5:// proxies; "Use the global update proxy" reuses the update proxy from System Settings. Without a proxy, HTTP channels follow HTTPS_PROXY and similar environment variables and email connects directly.
proxyChannelHelp: For networks where the notification service is only reachable through a proxy. Follows the global proxy in notification settings by default.
proxySmtpHelp: Email opens its TCP connection through the proxy: http(s) proxies use the CONNECT method (the proxy must allow the mail port), socks5 proxies resolve the server name on the proxy.
